methods.label: Track the sales, then subtract costs
methods.explanation:
Track the loaves remaining after each sale, since the afternoon fraction applies only to the unsold loaves.

In the morning Bridget sells \(48\cdot\frac12=24\) loaves, collecting \(24\cdot2.50=60\) dollars. This leaves \(24\) loaves.

In the afternoon she sells \(24\cdot\frac23=16\) loaves. Half of the original price is \(2.50\div2=1.25\) dollars, so these sales bring in \(16\cdot1.25=20\) dollars.

The remaining \(24-16=8\) loaves sell for one dollar each, bringing in another \(8\) dollars. Her total revenue is therefore
\[
60+20+8=88\text{ dollars}.
\]
Profit is revenue minus the cost of making all \(48\) loaves. That cost is \(48\cdot0.75=36\) dollars, so her profit is
\[
88-36=52\text{ dollars},
\]
choice E.
